name: Swedish Köttbullar
description: Köttbullar, Sweden's beloved meatballs, genuinely aren't originally Swedish at all - the recipe was brought back from Turkey by King Karl XII after his exile in Istanbul around 1713. Real technique seasons with nutmeg and allspice, and the complete real plate is never meatballs alone - real tradition serves them with cream gravy, lingonberry sauce, mashed potatoes, and pressed cucumber together.

ingredients_full.note: tbsp, standing in for lingonberry, for serving

steps_detailed: Mix the beef with the nutmeg, allspice, onion, egg, and breadcrumbs, kneading well.
Shape into small round meatballs.
Fry in the butter, turning, 8-9 minutes, until deeply browned and cooked through, then set aside.
Add the cream and broth to the same pan, and simmer 4-5 minutes into a gravy.
Serve the meatballs with the gravy and the cranberry sauce alongside, real tradition treating this as one complete plate.

name: Swedish Gravlax
description: Gravlax genuinely means 'buried salmon' in Swedish - medieval fishermen literally buried salted fish in sand to cure and preserve it, a technique since abandoned in favor of curing in the refrigerator instead. Real gravlax is never cooked or smoked, cured only with salt, sugar, and fresh dill, using fresh, high-quality salmon meant to be eaten raw.

ingredients_full.note: sushi-grade or previously frozen for food safety

ingredients.note: sushi-grade or previously frozen for food safety

steps_detailed: Mix the salt, sugar, dill, and pepper together.
Rub the mixture generously over the salmon flesh.
Wrap tightly in plastic wrap and refrigerate at least 24 hours, ideally 48, flipping once halfway through.
Rinse off the cure, pat dry, and slice thin against the grain to serve.

name: Swedish Pressed Cucumber (Pressgurka)
description: Pressgurka, a real vinegar-pressed cucumber salad, is the traditional accompaniment to köttbullar, real technique salting and pressing the cucumber to draw out excess water for a real crisp bite.
steps_detailed: Salt the cucumber slices and press under a plate for 20-30 minutes to draw out excess water.
Drain, then toss with the vinegar, sugar, and dill.

name: Swedish Kanelbullar (Cinnamon Buns)
description: Kanelbullar, real Swedish cinnamon buns, genuinely include real cardamom in the dough alongside the cinnamon filling, a distinctive Scandinavian touch missing from most Western cinnamon rolls.
steps_detailed: Mix the flour, half the butter, half the sugar, cardamom, and baking powder with a little milk into a soft dough.
Roll out into a rectangle, spread with the remaining butter, and sprinkle with the remaining sugar and cinnamon.
Roll up tightly and slice into rounds.
Bake at 375F (190C) for 15-18 minutes until golden.

name: Swedish Grilled Salmon
description: Grilled salmon, seasoned simply with dill, reflects Sweden's rich fishing tradition along its long coastline.
steps_detailed: Rub the salmon with the dill and lemon juice, and let sit 10 minutes.
Grill or broil, 4-5 minutes per side, until just cooked through.

name: Swedish Roasted Almonds
description: A simple roasted almond snack, common across Sweden.
steps_detailed: Toast the almonds in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring often, 4-5 minutes, until fragrant.

name: Swedish Beef and Vegetable Stew
description: A simple, hearty beef and vegetable stew, common Swedish home cooking outside the specific named dishes.
steps_detailed: Brown the beef with the onion, 8-9 minutes.
Add the carrot, potato, and tomatoes, and simmer 30-35 minutes until tender.

name: Swedish Gravlax Mustard Sauce (Hovmästarsås)
description: Hovmästarsås, a sweet mustard-dill sauce, is the real, traditional accompaniment to gravlax, real technique whisking the oil in gradually to build a smooth emulsion.
steps_detailed: Whisk the mustard, honey, and vinegar together.
Gradually whisk in the oil until a smooth emulsion forms.
Stir in the dill.
